title: Exercises for Knee Pain: What's Safe at Home
intro: When your knee hurts, light exercise without jumping and without deep squats is usually safer to try. The focus is on strengthening the muscles around the knee within a pain-free range.
muscles: Front thighs (quadriceps), back thighs, butt (glutes) and calves. These muscles help support your knees when you walk and climb stairs.
steps: Sit on a chair. Slowly straighten one leg, hold for 3 seconds, then lower it. Do this 8-10 times on each leg.
Lie on your back with one knee bent. Keep the other leg straight, tighten your thigh, lift it to the height of the bent knee, then slowly lower it. Do this 8 times.
Still lying down, with both knees bent. Squeeze your butt and lift your hips slightly (bridge), hold for 2 seconds, then lower down. Do this 8-10 times.
Stand holding the back of a chair. Slowly rise onto your toes, then lower your heels. Do this 10 times.
Sit down and stand up from a fairly high chair, using your hands to help if needed. Do this 5-8 times, and stop before it starts to hurt.
mistakes: Forcing your knee to bend too deep. Stay within a comfortable range, no need to go very low.
Letting your knees cave inwards when standing up from the chair. Keep your knees in line with your toes.
Stopping all movement completely out of fear. Light, controlled movement usually helps more than sitting still all day.
easier: Do all the moves sitting or lying down only, and reduce the reps to 5. For standing up from a chair, use a higher chair or add a cushion.
harder: Increase the reps to 12-15, or hold longer at the top (5 seconds). For the bridge, try lifting and holding for 5 seconds.
dose: 1-2 sets of each move, 3-4 times a week. One session of about 10-15 minutes is enough.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain, or your knee swells, locks or feels like it's giving way. If your knee was just injured, you recently had surgery, or the pain is getting worse, see a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: Is it normal to feel a bit sore after exercising?
faq.a: Mild muscle soreness that goes away in a day or two is usually okay. But sharp pain inside the joint, or pain that gets worse the next day, is a sign to cut back or stop.

faq.q: Can I walk if my knee hurts?
faq.a: Many people find walking on flat ground with comfortable shoes is fine. Start with 5-10 minutes and watch how your knee responds. Avoid hills or stairs for now if they trigger pain.

faq.q: Can losing a bit of weight help my knees?
faq.a: For some people, losing weight can reduce the load on the knees. The way to do it is to combine balanced eating with light exercise, not extreme dieting.
